# Technical Components and Requirements Model

The Technical Components and Requirements Model says how: the components, the requirements they realize and the goals they serve. The first diagram of each scope shows structure; the second traces each component, requirement and IS goal to the goals it serves.

Method: 4EM (Sandkuhl, Stirna, Persson and Wißotzki, *Enterprise Modeling: Tackling Business Challenges with the 4EM Method*, Springer 2014). Every element cites its source; `decided` means a source shows that the operator decided it.

Shifting one effect by three frames makes it fail and name the effect. *Why proposed:* Spec plan: spec 0001 and spec 0002 set out the one-frame tolerance. The operator has not decided the threshold, so confirm it. | proposed | serves: [Effects connect to produced events](goals.md#goal-reebeat-event-timing), [Check the written files, not the pipeline's memory](goals.md#goal-reebeat-verified-output) | [reebeat:docs/specs/0001-release-1-screenplay-to-deck-and-video.md:145][114], [reebeat:docs/specs/0002-explicit-anchors-and-syntax.md:128][115] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-tier-gate"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-tier-gate</code><br/>Requirement | **The package direction is enforced by a gate.** A package cannot depend on a tier it may not use, in its manifest or in an import, and no package directory can exist outside a tier. Quality: correctness. Scenario: A contributor makes the core import the services package. `bun run check:tiers` fails and names the edge. Adding a directory under `packages/` that is in no tier also fails. *Why proposed:* Observed in the repository: the tier gate and AGENTS.md describe this check. The operator decided the direction of dependency (spec 0001 line 234), not the gate, so confirm it. | proposed | serves: [A compiler whose structure prevents bad states](goals.md#goal-reebeat-correct-by-construction) | [reebeat:AGENTS.md:33][116], [reebeat:tools/quality/tiers.ts:41-48][117] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-extensibility"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-extensibility</code><br/>Requirement | **A new adapter needs no core change.** A plugin author adds an adapter by implementing a service's Layer and passing its contract suite. The name is then selectable, and the core, the program and the screenplay do not change. Quality: extensibility. Scenario: A plugin author writes a hosted speech adapter. It must pass the speech contract suite. Selecting it by name builds the story, and the manifest lists the adapter and what it sends out. Without its credential the build fails and falls back to nothing. *Why proposed:* Observed in the repository: AGENTS.md describes adding an adapter. The operator decided plugins are supported and every adapter passes a contract suite, but the adapter shape is marked proposed, so confirm this scenario. | proposed | serves: [Plugins and a render-engine SDK](goals.md#goal-reebeat-plugin-sdk) | [reebeat:docs/design/open-core-boundary.md:24][118], [reebeat:AGENTS.md:61][119] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-licensing"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-licensing</code><br/>Requirement | **Licences are checked before a dependency lands.** Every manifest declares Apache-2.0, and every locked package has a recorded licence on the allowlist. GPL, AGPL, SSPL and unknown licences are rejected. Quality: licensing. Scenario: A contributor adds a package to `bun.lock` without recording its licence. `bun run test` fails and names the package. Adding a GPL package fails too. *Why proposed:* Spec plan: spec 0008 sets out the licence gate and its allowlist. The operator decided Apache-2.0 (log:44), not the gate, so confirm it. | proposed | serves: [License the compiler and its formats under Apache-2.0](goals.md#goal-reebeat-apache-licence) | [reebeat:docs/specs/0008-apache-2-licence.md:42][120], [reebeat:AGENTS.md:30][121] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-usability"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-usability</code><br/>Requirement | **Errors say how to fix the source.** Each error names the file and line, what was found, what was expected and the nearest valid form. Old forms are rejected with the replacement in the message. Quality: usability. Scenario: An author writes the old `[[next]]` cue. The parser stops, names the line and shows the form to use instead. A person who rewrote a story from the messages alone built and checked it. *Why proposed:* Spec plan: spec 0002 sets out the error format. The operator has not decided it, so confirm it. | proposed | serves: [An explicit source nobody can misread](goals.md#goal-reebeat-explicit-source) | [reebeat:docs/specs/0002-explicit-anchors-and-syntax.md:17][122], [reebeat:docs/specs/0002-explicit-anchors-and-syntax.md:190][123] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-reliability"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-reliability</code><br/>Requirement | **A failed build leaves no accepted output.** A speech cache miss with models absent, an alignment below the threshold, and a capture timeout each stop the build with a typed error. No directory remains that `check` would accept. Quality: reliability. Scenario: A developer deletes one speech cache entry and builds without refreshing. The build stops with a cache-miss error that names the Line. The output directory holds no partial build. *Why proposed:* Spec plan: spec 0001 falsifier F12 sets out the three failure cases. The operator has not decided them, so confirm it. | proposed | serves: [A compiler whose structure prevents bad states](goals.md#goal-reebeat-correct-by-construction) | [reebeat:docs/specs/0001-release-1-screenplay-to-deck-and-video.md:156][124], [reebeat:packages/pipeline/src/buildProgram.ts:9-11][125] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-security"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-security</code><br/>Requirement | **Credentials never reach outputs.** Credentials are read from the environment inside the adapter. They never appear in a cache key, the Plan, the manifest or an output. Quality: security. Scenario: A test adapter needs a credential from the environment. Without it the build fails and names the requirement and writes nothing. With it, a canary value never appears in any written file. *Why proposed:* Spec plan: design R3 rule 3 and spec 0001 set out the credential handling. The operator has not decided it, so confirm it. | proposed | serves: [Every build says what leaves the machine](goals.md#goal-reebeat-visible-egress) | [reebeat:docs/design/keyframe-engine.md:1242][126], [reebeat:docs/specs/0001-release-1-screenplay-to-deck-and-video.md:262][23] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-incremental"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-incremental</code><br/>Requirement | **An edit rebuilds only what it changes.** After an edit, the build redoes only the work that depends on it, and the result is byte-identical to a cold build. Quality: performance. Scenario: An author changes one narration line in a story. Only that Line's speech and the render segments that depend on its length are rebuilt. The output equals a cold build of the new story. This is planned and not built. *Why proposed:* The operator asked for fast incremental builds (log:10, log:62). The measure and the design come from issue #9, which the operator has not decided. | proposed | serves: [Fast, incremental and reactive builds](goals.md#goal-reebeat-incremental-builds) | [log L10][14], [log L62][1], [issue reebeat#9][15] |
| <a id="req-reebeat-nfr-portability"></a><code>req-reebeat-nfr-portability</code><br/>Requirement | **Release 1 runs on Linux inside devenv.** A build runs on Linux with the pinned devenv tools. Other systems need their own Chromium, and Windows and macOS are not supported. Quality: portability. Scenario: A contributor clones the repository on Linux and runs the journey inside `devenv shell`. It builds and checks the story. On another system the contributor sets the Chromium path and installs the other tools by hand. *Why open:* Spec 0001 lists Windows and macOS as not in scope for release 1. Whether the supported platforms grow is the operator's choice, and published packages may widen it. | open | serves: [Reproducible builds](goals.md#goal-reebeat-reproducible-builds) | [reebeat:README.md:12][127], [reebeat:docs/specs/0001-release-1-screenplay-to-deck-and-video.md:189][128], [reebeat:devenv.nix:3][129] |

The PR body reports three passing runs (12 of 12 checks) on an earlier head, and later states that a measurement on an overloaded host is inconclusive, not pass or fail. The gate runs locally only. The operator must confirm it as the standing gate. | proposed | serves: [Prove interaction in a real browser](goals.md#goal-flow-browser-proof) | [pr foldkit-flow#4][225] |
| <a id="req-flow-perf-drag"></a><code>req-flow-perf-drag</code><br/>Requirement | **Dragging stays fast at 500 nodes and 700 edges.** Dragging one node of 500 nodes and 700 edges has a median p95 scripting time per pointer move under 8 ms. At least 95 percent of frame intervals are within 33.5 ms. Quality: performance. Scenario: A person drags one node of the Large graph (500 nodes, 700 edges) for 150 pointer moves, three times, in headless Chromium on the production build. The median of the three p95 scripting times per move is under 8 ms, and 95 percent of frame intervals are within 33.5 ms. Ten wheel steps change no node or edge. *Why proposed:* The numbers are the gate in spec 0001 (J9). The PR reports a median of 4.31 to 5.76 ms over three runs on a loaded host. They are the author's report. The operator must confirm the budget. | proposed | serves: [Stay smooth at 500 nodes and 700 edges](goals.md#goal-flow-performance) | [pr foldkit-flow#4][225] |
| <a id="req-flow-a11y-keyboard"></a><code>req-flow-a11y-keyboard</code><br/>Requirement | **Keyboard-only use with announcements.** Selecting, moving, deleting and clearing nodes works with the keyboard alone, and results are announced to assistive technology. Creating or reconnecting a connection, and using the minimap, are not specified. Quality: accessibility. Scenario: A keyboard-only user presses Tab to reach a node, Enter to select it, an arrow key to move it by 10, Shift and an arrow to move it by 40, Escape to clear, Enter again and Delete to remove it. The canvas has role application, each node has role group and a name, and a polite live region says what happened. *Why proposed:* PR #4 plan: the steps are the PR's keyboard journey and README accessibility section. Creating a connection by keyboard is not built. The PR does not say that reconnecting an edge or using the minimap works by keyboard, so those stay open. The operator must confirm the target. | proposed | serves: [Keyboard-accessible graph editing](goals.md#goal-flow-keyboard-access) | [pr foldkit-flow#4][225] |
| <a id="req-flow-correct-lifetimes"></a><code>req-flow-correct-lifetimes</code><br/>Requirement | **Controllers never leak after unmount.** Every controller is destroyed when its Mount is released, and no listener it added remains. Quality: correctness. Scenario: A test mounts the Flow, presses a handle before the drag threshold, then disposes the runtime. Every created controller is destroyed once, and no document or window listener from the library remains. *Why proposed:* Spec 0001 sets falsifier J8 and its round-1 fix; absent at the pinned commit 5dd44a9 (PR #4 has since merged; see the tracker). The operator must confirm. | proposed | serves: [One felt journey works end to end](goals.md#goal-flow-first-journey) | [pr foldkit-flow#4][225], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:61][237] |
| <a id="req-flow-maintain-gates"></a><code>req-flow-maintain-gates</code><br/>Requirement | **Gates catch drift, dead code and copies.** Gates catch suppressions without a registry entry, unused code and copy-paste, and every gate runs locally and in CI. Quality: maintainability. Scenario: A contributor pastes a 40-token block twice and `bun run cpd` fails. A contributor adds a suppression directive with no registry entry and `bun run check:exceptions` fails. *Why proposed:* Observed in the repository: AGENTS.md describes these gates. No operator line decides them. The operator must confirm. | proposed | serves: [Every change travels spec, code, PR](goals.md#goal-flow-lifecycle) | [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:43][242], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:47-48][243] |
| <a id="req-flow-maintain-tiers"></a><code>req-flow-maintain-tiers</code><br/>Requirement | **Tools, packages and apps stay separate.** Apps, packages and tools are separate workspaces. The app depends on the library and tools depend on neither. Quality: maintainability. Scenario: A reader lists the workspaces and finds apps, packages and tools apart. The example app declares the library as a workspace dependency, and the library does not depend on the app. *Why proposed:* The layout is the same at the pin. No gate enforces the direction, so the scenario is a reading check. The operator must confirm and may add a gate. | proposed | serves: [A generic library with no product logic](goals.md#goal-flow-generic-library) | [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:21-30][244], [foldkit-flow:package.json:5-9][245], [foldkit-flow:apps/example/package.json:17][227] |
| <a id="req-flow-licence-hygiene"></a><code>req-flow-licence-hygiene</code><br/>Requirement | **MIT library, xyflow credited, no copyleft dependency.** The library is MIT licensed with xyflow's notice kept. It does not depend on ELK.js or another copyleft package. Quality: licensing. Scenario: A reader opens LICENSE, NOTICE and packages/flow/package.json. They find MIT, the xyflow copyright and licence, and no EPL or GPL dependency. *Why proposed:* The files show the state at the pin. No gate scans licences. The operator must confirm and may add a licence check before publishing. | proposed | serves: [Credit and respect xyflow](goals.md#goal-flow-respect-xyflow) | [foldkit-flow:LICENSE:1-3][246], [foldkit-flow:NOTICE:4-14][247], [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:30][248] |
| <a id="req-flow-effect-range-gated"></a><code>req-flow-effect-range-gated</code><br/>Requirement | **A new Effect minor cannot break the library.** A published package that uses an unstable or experimental Effect API cannot accept the next Effect minor, and a test fails if it does. Quality: reliability. Scenario: A contributor changes the library's Effect peer range to `^4.1.0` and imports an unstable API from the `effect` root. `bun run test` fails in the published-range test. *Why proposed:* Observed in the repository: the operator's cap rule (log line 55, AGENTS.md line 63) is decided, but the test that enforces it is spec 0000's design (falsifier F13). The operator must confirm it as a requirement. | proposed | serves: [Stay on supported Effect APIs and fix problems upstream](goals.md#goal-org-stay-on-supported-stack) | [foldkit-flow:AGENTS.md:63][249], [foldkit-flow:docs/specs/0000-development-lifecycle.md:89][250], [log L55][6] |
| <a id="req-flow-reproducible-toolchain"></a><code>req-flow-reproducible-toolchain</code><br/>Requirement | **The same Bun runs everywhere.** `vp run` and devenv use the same Bun version. Quality: reproducibility. Scenario: A contributor runs `vp exec -- bun --revision` and `bun --revision` in devenv. Both print the same version. The check does not show that every gate gives the same result in both. *Why open:* Issue #3 proposes this check and pinning Bun exactly. It is not fixed yet. | open | serves: [Reproducible builds](goals.md#goal-org-reproducible-builds) | [issue foldkit-flow#3][251], [foldkit-flow:package.json:43-47][252] |
| <a id="req-flow-portability-browsers"></a><code>req-flow-portability-browsers</code><br/>Requirement | **Supported browsers and input types.** The library states which browsers and input types it supports, and the journey covers them. Quality: portability. Scenario: The journey runs in each supported browser and input type and passes. Today it runs in one Chromium with mouse and keyboard. *Why open:* No source sets a support target. PR #4 lists Firefox, WebKit and touch as not run. The operator must set the target. | open | serves: [Prove interaction in a real browser](goals.md#goal-flow-browser-proof) | [pr foldkit-flow#4][225] |

## Rejected alternatives

Components that were considered and rejected. They serve no goal; the problems that hinder them say why.

| Alternative | Why rejected | Status | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="comp-org-react-core-compiler"></a>React's core as the compiler core (rejected) | React has no whole-timeline planning. The scheduler follows the wall clock. A reproducible build needs time that the compiler controls. Keys only identify siblings, but a story needs identity across Scenes. One host tree does not fit several artifacts and render engines. React keeps incremental state inside one process, not in persistent traces. It has no notion of audio. | decided | [log L64][8] |

## Quality goals

The non-functional requirements with a stated quality and scenario (arc42 section 10, quality scenarios).

| Scope | Quality | Requirement | Scenario | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| org | maintainability | Generated documents never drift from the model. A test fails when a committed generated document differs from what the generator makes from the model. | Someone edits a generated page by hand. The drift test fails in CI and names the page. | proposed |
| org | performance | The Build rebuilds only what an edit changes. The Build is an incremental graph with dynamic dependencies and early cutoff. | An author edits one line of narration. Only the speech, the timing and the frames that depend on that line are rebuilt; the rest comes from the cache. | proposed |
| org | reproducibility | Persistent traces are content-addressed. The Build keeps persistent traces that are addressed by content. | The same story is built twice, once warm and once cold. The two artifacts are byte-identical. | proposed |
| reebeat | reproducibility | Two builds are identical. The same source and cache, built twice on the same machine, give identical decoded video frames and identical decoded audio samples. Container bytes are compared and the result is recorded. | A developer builds `stories/same-id` twice with the same speech cache. `reebeat journey` compares every decoded frame hash and the decoded audio hash. The check passes when all agree. Adding random jitter to the clock makes it fail and name the first differing frame. | proposed |
| reebeat | accessibility | Artifacts serve different audiences. Subtitles and speaker notes carry the narration text exactly. Captions, audio description and reduced-motion variants for the other audiences follow in issue #12. | A viewer who cannot hear opens the Video and reads the WebVTT subtitles. The check confirms one cue per Line with text equal to the narration. A viewer who prefers reduced motion gets a variant with cuts or crossfades, which is planned and not built. | proposed |
| reebeat | correctness | Effects appear within one frame of their anchor. Every effect shows in the written video, and sounds in the written audio, within one frame of the frame its anchor resolves to. | A story has a sound anchored to the start of a transition. After a build, the check measures the first changed frame and the sound onset in the files. The check passes when both are within one frame. Shifting one effect by three frames makes it fail and name the effect. | proposed |
| reebeat | correctness | The package direction is enforced by a gate. A package cannot depend on a tier it may not use, in its manifest or in an import, and no package directory can exist outside a tier. | A contributor makes the core import the services package. `bun run check:tiers` fails and names the edge. Adding a directory under `packages/` that is in no tier also fails. | proposed |
| reebeat | extensibility | A new adapter needs no core change. A plugin author adds an adapter by implementing a service's Layer and passing its contract suite. The name is then selectable, and the core, the program and the screenplay do not change. | A plugin author writes a hosted speech adapter. It must pass the speech contract suite. Selecting it by name builds the story, and the manifest lists the adapter and what it sends out. Without its credential the build fails and falls back to nothing. | proposed |
| reebeat | licensing | Licences are checked before a dependency lands. Every manifest declares Apache-2.0, and every locked package has a recorded licence on the allowlist. GPL, AGPL, SSPL and unknown licences are rejected. | A contributor adds a package to `bun.lock` without recording its licence. `bun run test` fails and names the package. Adding a GPL package fails too. | proposed |
| reebeat | usability | Errors say how to fix the source. Each error names the file and line, what was found, what was expected and the nearest valid form. Old forms are rejected with the replacement in the message. | An author writes the old `[[next]]` cue. The parser stops, names the line and shows the form to use instead. A person who rewrote a story from the messages alone built and checked it. | proposed |
| reebeat | reliability | A failed build leaves no accepted output. A speech cache miss with models absent, an alignment below the threshold, and a capture timeout each stop the build with a typed error. No directory remains that `check` would accept. | A developer deletes one speech cache entry and builds without refreshing. The build stops with a cache-miss error that names the Line. The output directory holds no partial build. | proposed |
| reebeat | security | Credentials never reach outputs. Credentials are read from the environment inside the adapter. They never appear in a cache key, the Plan, the manifest or an output. | A test adapter needs a credential from the environment. Without it the build fails and names the requirement and writes nothing. With it, a canary value never appears in any written file. | proposed |
| reebeat | performance | An edit rebuilds only what it changes. After an edit, the build redoes only the work that depends on it, and the result is byte-identical to a cold build. | An author changes one narration line in a story. Only that Line's speech and the render segments that depend on its length are rebuilt. The output equals a cold build of the new story. This is planned and not built. | proposed |
| reebeat | portability | Release 1 runs on Linux inside devenv. A build runs on Linux with the pinned devenv tools. Other systems need their own Chromium, and Windows and macOS are not supported. | A contributor clones the repository on Linux and runs the journey inside `devenv shell`. It builds and checks the story. On another system the contributor sets the Chromium path and installs the other tools by hand. | open |
| studio | correctness | A preview frame equals the Video frame. The in-browser preview at a frame equals the Video's frame at the same time. | For the first frame, a mid-transition frame, a frame inside a focus ring and the last frame of the same-id story, the preview at seek(frame) and the Video frame are byte for byte equal after PNG decode, on the same Chromium build. | proposed |
| studio | reliability | The free journey works offline. With the network off, the free journey still works and the page requests nothing but its own static files. | With the network off and the static assets served, a person opens a story, sees the graph and timeline, scrubs, edits one property and undoes it. The page makes no request except for its own files. | proposed |
| studio | accessibility | Every editor region has an accessible name. The editor has one h1, and each region and the inspector has an accessible name. The inspector button exposes its state with aria-expanded. | A screen reader user lists the landmarks and finds Story graph, Preview, Timeline and Inspector by name. The Hide inspector button reports aria-expanded true while the inspector shows, and false when it is hidden. | proposed |
| studio | correctness | A merged story is valid or refused. After any merge, the shared story is a valid story. No merge stores an invalid one. | Two peers edit a story at the same time and then merge. If the merged document does not decode as a valid story, the server refuses it and names the reason. Over the 66 valid spike outcomes, it refused none. | proposed |
| studio | reproducibility | The same updates give the same story on every peer. Updates replayed in any order give the same projected story text on every peer. | Replay the same updates in 200 random orders into fresh replicas. Every replica gives the same story text, with 0 differing texts, on Bun and on Node. | proposed |
| studio | performance | Edit latency and edge cost are not yet measured. An edit must show in the preview within a latency budget, and the sync gate must start and run within a measured size. At the pinned commit neither number exists. | Milestone M0 measures the compile and render time of the same-id story in a browser and sets the budget for one edit. A Cloudflare edge run measures the gate's bundle size, cold start and load with many sockets. | open |
| studio | security | The binary serves only on loopback and only reads. The binary binds a loopback address, answers GET and HEAD only and refuses a path outside its embedded files. | A client on a non-loopback address of the same machine cannot connect. A POST returns 405. A request path with dot-dot segments reaches no file outside the embedded set, although a normalised path can answer with an embedded file. | proposed |
| studio | portability | The binary runs on five targets. The release builds binaries for Linux x64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x64, and Windows x64. No Linux binary names a path in the Nix store. | On the runners that run the full smoke (Linux x64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x64), the binary starts, serves and exits cleanly on a stop signal. On Windows only the start-and-check step runs. A file-type check fails any Linux binary that names /nix/store. | proposed |
| studio | licensing | Every distributed artifact has a known licence. Before studio distributes a binary, the licence of studio and of any bundled third-party code is known. At the pinned commit studio's licence is undecided, and its binary does not bundle ffmpeg. | Before a release, the operator has chosen a licence and added a LICENSE file. A binary that bundles ffmpeg with libx264 has had its GPL terms reviewed. | open |
| studio | maintainability | One command runs every gate. The ready command runs format, lint, types, the exception check, tests, build, dead code, duplication and secret scans. CI runs the same gates. | On a clean tree, the ready command exits 0. Adding a lint suppression with no registry entry makes the exception check fail and name the file and line. | proposed |
| studio | extensibility | Users extend studio with their own agents and plugins. Studio stays modular so users add agents and plugins without changing studio's code. | A user connects an agent that studio did not ship, through the published tool protocol, and the agent edits a story with the same tools the editor uses. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | performance | Dragging stays fast at 500 nodes and 700 edges. Dragging one node of 500 nodes and 700 edges has a median p95 scripting time per pointer move under 8 ms. At least 95 percent of frame intervals are within 33.5 ms. | A person drags one node of the Large graph (500 nodes, 700 edges) for 150 pointer moves, three times, in headless Chromium on the production build. The median of the three p95 scripting times per move is under 8 ms, and 95 percent of frame intervals are within 33.5 ms. Ten wheel steps change no node or edge. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | accessibility | Keyboard-only use with announcements. Selecting, moving, deleting and clearing nodes works with the keyboard alone, and results are announced to assistive technology. Creating or reconnecting a connection, and using the minimap, are not specified. | A keyboard-only user presses Tab to reach a node, Enter to select it, an arrow key to move it by 10, Shift and an arrow to move it by 40, Escape to clear, Enter again and Delete to remove it. The canvas has role application, each node has role group and a name, and a polite live region says what happened. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | correctness | Controllers never leak after unmount. Every controller is destroyed when its Mount is released, and no listener it added remains. | A test mounts the Flow, presses a handle before the drag threshold, then disposes the runtime. Every created controller is destroyed once, and no document or window listener from the library remains. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | maintainability | Gates catch drift, dead code and copies. Gates catch suppressions without a registry entry, unused code and copy-paste, and every gate runs locally and in CI. | A contributor pastes a 40-token block twice and `bun run cpd` fails. A contributor adds a suppression directive with no registry entry and `bun run check:exceptions` fails. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | maintainability | Tools, packages and apps stay separate. Apps, packages and tools are separate workspaces. The app depends on the library and tools depend on neither. | A reader lists the workspaces and finds apps, packages and tools apart. The example app declares the library as a workspace dependency, and the library does not depend on the app. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | reproducibility | The same Bun runs everywhere. `vp run` and devenv use the same Bun version. | A contributor runs `vp exec -- bun --revision` and `bun --revision` in devenv. Both print the same version. The check does not show that every gate gives the same result in both. | open |
| foldkit-flow | licensing | MIT library, xyflow credited, no copyleft dependency. The library is MIT licensed with xyflow's notice kept. It does not depend on ELK.js or another copyleft package. | A reader opens LICENSE, NOTICE and packages/flow/package.json. They find MIT, the xyflow copyright and licence, and no EPL or GPL dependency. | proposed |
| foldkit-flow | reliability | A new Effect minor cannot break the library. A published package that uses an unstable or experimental Effect API cannot accept the next Effect minor, and a test fails if it does. | A contributor changes the library's Effect peer range to `^4.1.0` and imports an unstable API from the `effect` root. `bun run test` fails in the published-range test. | proposed |
